title: Signed: Yoshiki Partners With BMG for Distribution, Virtual Riot Pacts With MLennial for Management
summary: Other recent signings include Virtual Riot, Oso Oso, Chase Wright, Mathias Lattin and Maggie Antone.
contentText:
Composer, pianist, drummer and recording artist Yoshiki , the frontman of X Japan, signed a global distribution and publishing admin agreement (ex-Japan) with BMG via his record label, Melodee. The agreement kicks off with the release of “Forever Love (Live),” Yoshiki’s new collab with Josh Groban, recorded live at Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles. It also covers Yoshiki’s solo album, Eternal Melody , and X Japan albums released from 1993 onward, including Art of Life and Dahlia .

“Bringing YOSHIKI’s recorded music and publishing administration together with BMG’s global infrastructure, the comprehensive agreement marks a major expansion of his worldwide music activities and the beginning of one of the most ambitious creative chapters of his career,” reads a press release about the deal.

“I’ve always believed that music has no borders. I’m now entering one of the most ambitious and creative chapters of my career, with new projects that bring together rock, pop, classical and contemporary music in ways I have never explored before,” said Yoshiki in a statement. “I’m thrilled to partner with BMG to bring this vision to the world. ‘Forever Love’ with Josh Groban marks the beginning-but this partnership represents something much bigger for the future.”

“YOSHIKI is a true global artist whose creativity, vision, and connection with fans transcend genres and borders,” added Michael Kachko , senior vp of BMG. “We are proud to partner with him at BMG to support and amplify this next chapter on a worldwide scale.” — Chris Eggertsen
